title: Client-Side Rendering
body:
The server sends a nearly empty HTML shell plus a JavaScript bundle; the browser then runs that JS, fetches data as [[JSON]] from an [[API]], and builds the [[DOM]] itself. This is how a single-page app such as a [[React]] SPA works — you assemble the plate at your own table from raw ingredients.

All of that work happens on **your machine**. The trade-offs: navigation after the first load feels instant because only data moves, not whole pages, but the initial load is slower (blank screen until the bundle downloads, parses, and runs), and anything depending on content being present in the initial HTML — some crawlers, link previews — sees an empty page. Compare [[Server-Side Rendering]].
